fractal_dimension — 2D features op

• Data kinds: image → feature

• Call: fullseye.apply(img, "fractal_dimension", a=0.5, b=0.5) (the 2-D model is one image plus two scalar knobs a,b∈[0,1])

*The figure is the actual output on a synthetic 128×128 input. Left: input, right: output. Point clouds are drawn as a top-down scatter (brightness = z), 1-D series as a line plot, volumes as the maximum-intensity projection along z, videos as the middle frame, complex images as magnitude; return values that are not pictures are shown as the values themselves.*

Sweeping knob a (0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9, the other knob at its default):

▸ fractal_dimension: knob a sweep (docs site)

*Knob b does not change the output (measured: identical at 0.1 / 0.5 / 0.9).*

Usage

Minkowski–Bouligand (box-counting) fractal dimension, which measures the complexity of a texture.

Binarize with the required threshold a and define the structure for box sizes s = 1, 2, 4, …. Count the number N(s) of containing s×s boxes'' and perform least squares regression of log N(s) on log(1/s). Returns the slope (Mandelbrot 1982). Linear structure is ~1, area filling the plane is ~2, self Similar edges are intermediate non-integers (log 3 / log 2 ≈ 1.585 for Sierpinski triangles). surface It can be used for inexpensive complexity features such as roughness, tissue texture, topography, and fracture surfaces.

The filled area is slightly less than 2 due to finite resolution (the known box saturates at coarse scales). underestimation). a is the binarization threshold, b is not used. No structure/1 Can only take scale Returns 0 if
